analysis: The PR changes only documentation comments. EngineV2Bridge.swift lines 132-136 (head) reword the kvBytesPerToken doc to refer to EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken and observed native per-layer K/V types. EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift lines 201-203 (head) reword the doc for nativeKVBytesPerToken as a fallback that over-reserves bf16 rows. Base and head shift the remaining code by one line and are otherwise identical. That covers the init, the prefix-cache store acceptance checks, the SSD cache wiring, the pending/cancel bookkeeping and the test seams. No executable logic, key handling, authorization, cache-scope derivation, TTL or encryption behavior changed. Relevant threat T-041 touches EngineV2Bridge.swift via the SSD cache staging wiring, and that wiring is unchanged. The comment claims production slots always supply observed native types, which is a contract this PR does not show. The slotKVBytesPerToken implementation and its callers are outside the supplied evidence. If that claim were wrong, the fallback would over-reserve, not under-reserve, since the comment says it over-reserves bf16 rows. That would be an availability and capacity concern rather than a confidentiality one, and is unverified. Nothing in this diff changes a security conclusion. Integration should confirm that EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken exists and is used in production, but this is not a security regression.
